questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was a rather big city close to the sea and a city with a lot of history and culture. I had already been to Valencia, and I liked the city a lot.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Studying abroad was challenging, and it takes a lot to get used to a completely different educational system.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult, and definitely took more effort than expected.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I didn't receive much assistance other than at a very simple "welcome-meeting" for the Erasmus students. Apart from that we were pretty much left to figure things out ourselves. Whenever I emailed the study guidance office of my faculty in Valencia, it would take them weeks to answer, and the few times I went to the office, they would ask me to leave and not come back, because they couldn't do anything to help me with my questions. Questions concerning my schedule, subjects and other practical university things. 
The lack of assistance or help resulted in a lot of confusion, not just for me, but for a lot of the Erasmus students. I missed the first 1,5 months of lessons in one of my subjects, because the administration at the university was so slow, and they didn't assign me to the classes, before much later. 
My home university (University of Copenhagen) wasn't of much help either. It also took them a long time to respond to on emails, so I truly felt that I was on my own with all my doubts and questions, and that was quite frustrating and demotivating.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: If I could have chosen to rate it 0, I would have done that. The orientation was very insufficient, and as an Erasmus student you were just left to figure out things yourself.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, but only if you are able to speak the language of the country.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a cheaper option.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very confusing, poorly managed and it took way to much time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful because it turned out that almost all the classes I had noted in my preapproval werent offered that semester, so I had to research all over and find new classes that I was less motivated to have.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lower your expectations, expect that things will not turn out as you have prepared them to do. You will have to be pragmatic and ready to change your schedule, when you arrive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was very different from how Danish education works. It felt like being back in high school.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In UCPH I feel that the students have way more autonomy and responsibility for their own learning. In Spain the lessons are more teacher-controlled. In Denmark the students are encouraged to think critically and use their own critical sense, but in Spain you are not supposed to do that, and that was a big challenge for me.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Norms and correct usage of Spanish. Literature and Modernity in Latin America. American Spanish. Spanish for foreigners. English language 5.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Norms and correct usage of Spanish. American Spanish.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult. The culture was very different from Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join sport teams or other social clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I often felt sexually discriminated in public, getting whistled at or looked at, followed by strangers etc. That was a challenge.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated how easy it was to meet new people in Spain (not necesarily other students), but it was quite easy meeting people, because the Spanish people in general are very open and social.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Don't go for the academic opportunities. 2. Spend time on finding a good and safe place to live, it is a good investment, when staying in a new country. 3. Maybe don't do a full semester, but just 15/20 ECTS points - a lot of Erasmus students do this, which gives them more time to explore and have fun, while they are abroad.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got to speak a lot of Spanish, which was the main reason for going.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding motivation in a radically different school system that didn't seem to want you there or help you, when you needed help.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
